title: Prospective clinical study on sexuality in neurodivergent individuals - SENSE: Sexuality and Neurodiversity Symptoms & Empirical Research
summary:
This study investigates differences in sexuality, sexual orientation, gender identity, risk behavior, and psychological characteristics among individuals with autism (ASD), ADHD, and people without these diagnoses.
Using a smartphone app, participants complete anonymous questionnaires regularly over a period of six months. This allows researchers to capture changes and developments in everyday life.
The aim of the study is to better understand differences between the groups and to examine whether the method of recruitment (online versus in person) influences the results. The study is conducted solely for research purposes; no treatment or diagnostic procedures are involved.

interventions.name:
Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD)
(App-based questionnaires and questions on sexuality, sexual orientation, and gender identity over a total period of 6 months)
Individuals with Attention Deficit (Hyperactivity) Disorder (ADHD) (App-based questionnaires and questions on sexuality, sexual orientation, and gender identity over a total period of 6 months)

Individuals without ADHD or ASD (healthy control group)
(App-based questionnaires and questions on sexuality, sexual orientation, and gender identity over a total period of 6 months)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants aged 18–65 years with either a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder or attention deficit disorder will be included. In addition, age- and education-matched control participants will be recruited. Only individuals with sufficient German language proficiency to independently complete the German-language online questionnaires will be eligible for inclusion.
Exclusion criteria:
Severe intellectual disability, serious and acute physical or mental illness, such as an acute psychosis, brain injury, Alzheimer’s disease, or a severe bacterial infection requiring immediate treatment, and insufficient German language skills.
